import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest' import { parseLighterPackHtml, parseLighterPackUrl } from './lighterpack' describe('LighterPack Parser', () => { describe('parseLighterPackHtml', () => { it('should parse basic LighterPack HTML structure', () => { const html = ` Test Loadout

    • Shelter

    • Tent Ultralight Tent 2 lb 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(1) expect(result.data[0]).toMatchObject({ description: 'Ultralight Tent', // description from lpDescription span weight_g: 907, // 2 lb = 907g weight_display_unit: 'lb', item_type: 'Tent', // name maps to item_type consumable: false }) }) it('should handle mixed weight units correctly', () => { const html = `

    • Gear

    • Item1 100 g 1
    • Item2 5.5 oz 1
    • Item3 1.3125 lb 1
    • Item4 0.5 kg 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(4) // Check weight conversions and unit preservation expect(result.data[0].weight_g).toBe(100) expect(result.data[0].weight_display_unit).toBe('g') expect(result.data[1].weight_g).toBe(156) // 5.5 * 28.3495 ≈ 156 expect(result.data[1].weight_display_unit).toBe('oz') expect(result.data[2].weight_g).toBe(595) // 1.3125 lb * 453.592 ≈ 595 expect(result.data[2].weight_display_unit).toBe('lb') expect(result.data[3].weight_g).toBe(500) // 0.5 kg = 500g expect(result.data[3].weight_display_unit).toBe('kg') }) it('should detect consumable flags from lpActive class', () => { const html = `

    • Food

    • Regular Item 150 g 1
    • Consumable Item 500 g 3
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(2) // First item should not be consumable expect(result.data[0].consumable).toBe(false) // Second item should be consumable based on lpActive class expect(result.data[1].consumable).toBe(true) }) it('should extract URLs from name anchors', () => { const html = `

    • Gear

    • Tent Ultralight Shelter 100 g
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(1) expect(result.data[0].url).toBe('https://example.com/tent') expect(result.data[0].description).toBe('Ultralight Shelter') // description from lpDescription span expect(result.data[0].item_type).toBe('Tent') // name becomes item_type }) it('should extract prices when present', () => { const html = `

    • Gear

    • Expensive Item $299.95 100 g 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(1) expect(result.data[0].price).toBe(299.95) }) it('should map name to item_type directly', () => { const testCases = [ { name: 'Tent', expected: 'Tent' }, { name: 'Sleeping Bag', expected: 'Sleeping Bag' }, { name: 'Water Filter', expected: 'Water Filter' }, { name: 'Hiking Boots', expected: 'Hiking Boots' } ] testCases.forEach(({ name, expected }) => { const html = `

    • Gear

    • ${name} 100 g 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.data[0].item_type).toBe(expected) expect(result.data[0].description).toBe(expected) // No lpDescription, so name becomes description }) }) it('should handle empty HTML gracefully', () => { const html = 'Empty List' const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(false) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(0) expect(result.errors).toContain('No lpCategories unordered list found') expect(result.metadata?.listName).toBe('Empty List') }) it('should extract metadata correctly', () => { const html = ` My Ultralight Loadout

    • Gear

    • Item1 100 g 2
    • Item2 50 g 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.metadata).toEqual({ listName: 'My Ultralight Loadout', itemCount: 2, totalWeight: 150 // 100g + 50g }) }) it('should handle malformed HTML without crashing', () => { const html = 'content' const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) // Should not throw and should provide useful error info expect(result).toBeDefined() expect(Array.isArray(result.data)).toBe(true) expect(Array.isArray(result.errors)).toBe(true) }) it('should handle real-world LighterPack HTML', () => { // Test with actual LighterPack HTML structure const html = ` Vaunted UL Loadout

Vaunted UL Loadout

    • Shelter

    • Tent Big Agnes Copper Spur HV UL + Stakes $549.95 42.5 oz 1
` const result = parseLighterPackHtml(html) expect(result.success).toBe(true) expect(result.data).toHaveLength(1) expect(result.data[0]).toMatchObject({ description: 'Big Agnes Copper Spur HV UL + Stakes', // description from lpDescription span weight_g: 1205, // 42.5 oz weight_display_unit: 'oz', item_type: 'Tent', // name maps to item_type price: 549.95 }) }) }) describe('parseLighterPackUrl', () => { it('should reject invalid URLs', async () => { const result = await parseLighterPackUrl('https://example.com/test') expect(result.success).toBe(false) expect(result.errors).toContain('Invalid LighterPack URL format. Expected: https://lighterpack.com/r/[ID]') }) it('should accept valid LighterPack URLs', async () => { const result = await parseLighterPackUrl('https://lighterpack.com/r/abc123') // Currently returns an error because direct URL import isn't implemented expect(result.success).toBe(false) expect(result.errors).toContain('Direct URL import not yet implemented. Please use CSV export from LighterPack for now.') }) }) })

   - Fixed URL extraction from anchor tags in `lpName` spans
   - Fixed name extraction to handle both plain text and anchor tags
   - Fixed error messages to match expected text
   - Corrected description extraction from `lpDescription` spans

3. **Design Philosophy Changes:**
   - **Removed intelligent categorization** - parsers now preserve original data rather than performing smart transformations
   - **Removed automatic brand detection** - maintains data integrity by not guessing/inferring information
   - **Updated all related tests** to expect preserved original data instead of transformed data

**Final Result:**
- **22 test files** passing
- **242 tests** passing (3 skipped)

The parsers now follow a clean separation of concerns: they parse and validate data while preserving original information, leaving any intelligent transformations for higher-level application logic when explicitly needed.

- `/checkpoint` - Auto-generates commit message from changes

- **Duplicate Handling**: Smart merging with user choice

Push to main branch auto-deploys via Vercel. Environment variables must be configured in Vercel dashboard.

# ENG-002: Testing Specification
*BetterPack Engineering Specification - Testing Philosophy & Implementation Standards*

This specification outlines BetterPack's testing philosophy, framework choices, and implementation patterns that all development must follow.

## Philosophy

Our testing approach prioritizes **practical value over test coverage metrics**:

1. **Test behavior, not implementation** - Focus on what the user experiences
2. **Avoid brittle mocking** - Mock only external dependencies (APIs, databases)
3. **Write tests that catch real bugs** - Prioritize integration over isolated unit tests
4. **Keep tests simple and maintainable** - Complex test setups indicate code smells

## Testing Stack

### Unit & Integration Tests
- **Framework**: [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) - Fast, Vite-native testing
- **Component Testing**: [React Testing Library](https://testing-library.com/) - User-centric approach
- **DOM Setup**: jsdom environment for browser APIs
- **Test Utilities**: @testing-library/user-event for realistic interactions

### End-to-End Tests  
- **Framework**: [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) - Cross-browser E2E testing
- **Coverage**: Critical user journeys and edge cases
- **Environments**: Desktop (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) + Mobile (iOS, Android)

### CI/CD
- **GitHub Actions** - Automated testing on every push/PR
- **Parallel execution** - Fast feedback loops
- **Artifact storage** - Build outputs and test reports

## Test Organization

```
src/
├── components/
│   └── **/*.test.tsx          # Component tests alongside source
├── utils/
│   └── **/*.test.ts           # Utility function tests
├── test/
│   └── setup.ts               # Global test configuration
└── types/

tests/
└── e2e/
    └── **/*.spec.ts           # End-to-end test scenarios
```

## Running Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (watch mode)
npm test

# Unit tests (single run)  
npm run test:run

# Unit tests with coverage
npm run test:coverage

# Unit tests with UI
npm run test:ui

# E2E tests
npm run test:e2e

# E2E tests with UI
npm run test:e2e:ui
```

## Writing Good Tests

### Unit Tests

**✅ DO: Test public interfaces**
```typescript
// Good - tests behavior user cares about
it('should calculate total weight including quantity', () => {
  const items = [
    { weight_grams: 100, quantity: 2 },
    { weight_grams: 50, quantity: 1 }
  ]
  expect(calculateTotalWeight(items)).toBe(250)
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Test implementation details**  
```typescript
// Bad - brittle, tied to implementation
it('should call useState with correct initial value', () => {
  const spy = vi.spyOn(React, 'useState')
  render(<Component />)
  expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue)
})
```

### Component Tests

**✅ DO: Test user interactions**
```typescript
it('should add gear when form is submitted', async () => {
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const onAdd = vi.fn()
  
  render(<AddGearForm onAdd={onAdd} />)
  
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/name/i), 'Test Item')
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/weight/i), '100')
  await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /add gear/i }))
  
  expect(onAdd).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
    name: 'Test Item',
    weight_grams: 100,
    // ... other expected properties
  })
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Over-mock internal dependencies**
```typescript
// Bad - mocks everything, tests nothing real
vi.mock('../hooks/useGear')
vi.mock('../utils/weight')  
vi.mock('../components/Input')
// ... tests that verify mocks were called
```

### E2E Tests

**✅ DO: Test complete user journeys**
```typescript
test('user can create and view gear list', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/')
  
  // Add gear
  await page.click('[data-testid=add-gear]')
  await page.fill('[data-testid=gear-name]', 'My Tent')
  await page.fill('[data-testid=gear-weight]', '2.5')
  await page.click('[data-testid=submit]')
  
  // Verify in list
  await expect(page.locator('text=My Tent')).toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.locator('text=2.5')).toBeVisible()
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Test UI details that change frequently**
```typescript
// Bad - breaks when CSS classes change
await expect(page.locator('.btn-primary.rounded-md')).toHaveClass('bg-blue-500')
```

## Mocking Guidelines

### When TO Mock
- **External APIs** (Supabase, Sentry)
- **Browser APIs** (localStorage, geolocation)  
- **Third-party libraries** (payment processors)
- **Network requests** in unit tests

### When NOT To Mock
- **React hooks** (useState, useEffect)
- **Utility functions** you wrote
- **Component dependencies** in integration tests
- **DOM events** and user interactions

### Mocking Setup
Global mocks are configured in `src/test/setup.ts`:

```typescript
// Mock Supabase client
vi.mock('../lib/supabase', () => ({
  supabase: {
    // Simplified mock that returns predictable data
  }
}))
```

Per-test mocks when needed:
```typescript
// Override global mock for specific test
vi.mocked(supabase.from).mockReturnValueOnce({
  select: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ data: mockGearItems })
})
```

## Test Data Management

### Factories for Test Data
```typescript
// src/test/factories.ts
export const createGearItem = (overrides = {}) => ({
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  name: 'Test Gear',
  weight_grams: 100,
  category: 'Other',
  quantity: 1,
  worn: false,
  consumable: false,
  ...overrides
})
```

### Realistic Test Scenarios
```typescript
describe('Weight Calculations', () => {
  it('handles real backpacking gear weights', () => {
    const gear = [
      createGearItem({ name: 'Tent', weight_grams: 1200 }),
      createGearItem({ name: 'Sleeping Bag', weight_grams: 800 }),
      createGearItem({ name: 'Backpack', weight_grams: 1500, worn: true })
    ]
    
    expect(calculateBaseWeight(gear)).toBe(2000) // Excludes worn items
    expect(calculateTotalWeight(gear)).toBe(3500) // Includes all items
  })
})
```

## Coverage Guidelines

We aim for **meaningful coverage, not 100%**:

- **Critical paths**: Authentication, data persistence, calculations
- **Edge cases**: Error states, empty states, boundary conditions  
- **User workflows**: Complete feature interactions
- **Accessibility**: Screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation

Coverage thresholds (configured in `vite.config.ts`):
- **Statements**: 80%
- **Branches**: 75%  
- **Functions**: 80%
- **Lines**: 80%

## Performance Testing

### Load Testing (Future)
- Test gear list performance with 1000+ items
- Test search/filter responsiveness
- Mobile performance on slower devices

### Memory Leaks
- Monitor component cleanup in tests
- Test route transitions don't leak memory

## Accessibility Testing

E2E tests include basic accessibility checks:
```typescript
test('gear form is accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/gear/add')
  
  // Test keyboard navigation
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab')
  await expect(page.locator(':focus')).toHaveAttribute('data-testid', 'gear-name')
  
  // Test screen reader labels
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /gear name/i })).toBeVisible()
})
```

## Debugging Tests

### Interactive Debugging
```bash
# Debug unit tests with browser DevTools
npm run test:ui

# Debug E2E tests visually  
npm run test:e2e:ui

# Run E2E tests in headed mode
npx playwright test --headed --debug
```

### Common Issues

**Tests timing out**
```typescript
// Increase timeout for slow operations
test('slow operation', async ({ page }) => {
  test.setTimeout(60000) // 1 minute
  // ... test code
})
```

**Flaky E2E tests**
```typescript
// Wait for network requests to settle
await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')

// Use proper locators instead of timeouts
await expect(page.getByText('Success')).toBeVisible()
// Not: await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
```

## Best Practices Summary

1. **Start with E2E tests** for new features - they catch the most bugs
2. **Add unit tests** for complex business logic and utilities  
3. **Mock sparingly** - prefer real implementations when possible
4. **Test error states** - users will encounter them
5. **Keep tests focused** - one concept per test
6. **Use descriptive test names** - they serve as documentation
7. **Parallelize when possible** - faster feedback loops
8. **Review test failures immediately** - don't let them accumulate

## Resources

- [Testing Library Best Practices](https://testing-library.com/docs/guiding-principles)
- [Playwright Documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro)
- [Vitest Guide](https://vitest.dev/guide/)
- [Kent C. Dodds Testing Blog](https://kentcdodds.com/blog/common-mistakes-with-react-testing-library)

    { weight_grams: 50, quantity: 1 }
  ]
  expect(calculateTotalWeight(items)).toBe(250)
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Test implementation details**  
```typescript
// Bad - brittle, tied to implementation
it('should call useState with correct initial value', () => {
  const spy = vi.spyOn(React, 'useState')
  render(<Component />)
  expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue)
})
```

### Component Tests

**✅ DO: Test user interactions**
```typescript
it('should add gear when form is submitted', async () => {
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  const onAdd = vi.fn()
  
  render(<AddGearForm onAdd={onAdd} />)
  
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/name/i), 'Test Item')
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/weight/i), '100')
  await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /add gear/i }))
  
  expect(onAdd).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
    name: 'Test Item',
    weight_grams: 100,
    // ... other expected properties
  })
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Over-mock internal dependencies**
```typescript
// Bad - mocks everything, tests nothing real
vi.mock('../hooks/useGear')
vi.mock('../utils/weight')  
vi.mock('../components/Input')
// ... tests that verify mocks were called
```

### E2E Tests

**✅ DO: Test complete user journeys**
```typescript
test('user can create and view gear list', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/')
  
  // Add gear
  await page.click('[data-testid=add-gear]')
  await page.fill('[data-testid=gear-name]', 'My Tent')
  await page.fill('[data-testid=gear-weight]', '2.5')
  await page.click('[data-testid=submit]')
  
  // Verify in list
  await expect(page.locator('text=My Tent')).toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.locator('text=2.5')).toBeVisible()
})
```

**❌ DON'T: Test UI details that change frequently**
```typescript
// Bad - breaks when CSS classes change
await expect(page.locator('.btn-primary.rounded-md')).toHaveClass('bg-blue-500')
```

## Mocking Guidelines

### When TO Mock
- **External APIs** (Supabase, Sentry)
- **Browser APIs** (localStorage, geolocation)  
- **Third-party libraries** (payment processors)
- **Network requests** in unit tests

### When NOT To Mock
- **React hooks** (useState, useEffect)
- **Utility functions** you wrote
- **Component dependencies** in integration tests
- **DOM events** and user interactions

### Mocking Setup
Global mocks are configured in `src/test/setup.ts`:

```typescript
// Mock Supabase client
vi.mock('../lib/supabase', () => ({
  supabase: {
    // Simplified mock that returns predictable data
  }
}))
```

Per-test mocks when needed:
```typescript
// Override global mock for specific test
vi.mocked(supabase.from).mockReturnValueOnce({
  select: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ data: mockGearItems })
})
```

## Test Data Management

### Factories for Test Data
```typescript
// src/test/factories.ts
export const createGearItem = (overrides = {}) => ({
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  name: 'Test Gear',
  weight_grams: 100,
  category: 'Other',
  quantity: 1,
  worn: false,
  consumable: false,
  ...overrides
})
```

### Realistic Test Scenarios
```typescript
describe('Weight Calculations', () => {
  it('handles real backpacking gear weights', () => {
    const gear = [
      createGearItem({ name: 'Tent', weight_grams: 1200 }),
      createGearItem({ name: 'Sleeping Bag', weight_grams: 800 }),
      createGearItem({ name: 'Backpack', weight_grams: 1500, worn: true })
    ]
    
    expect(calculateBaseWeight(gear)).toBe(2000) // Excludes worn items
    expect(calculateTotalWeight(gear)).toBe(3500) // Includes all items
  })
})
```

## Coverage Guidelines

We aim for **meaningful coverage, not 100%**:

- **Critical paths**: Authentication, data persistence, calculations
- **Edge cases**: Error states, empty states, boundary conditions  
- **User workflows**: Complete feature interactions
- **Accessibility**: Screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation

Coverage thresholds (configured in `vite.config.ts`):
- **Statements**: 80%
- **Branches**: 75%  
- **Functions**: 80%
- **Lines**: 80%

## Performance Testing

### Load Testing (Future)
- Test gear list performance with 1000+ items
- Test search/filter responsiveness
- Mobile performance on slower devices

### Memory Leaks
- Monitor component cleanup in tests
- Test route transitions don't leak memory

## Accessibility Testing

E2E tests include basic accessibility checks:
```typescript
test('gear form is accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/gear/add')
  
  // Test keyboard navigation
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab')
  await expect(page.locator(':focus')).toHaveAttribute('data-testid', 'gear-name')
  
  // Test screen reader labels
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /gear name/i })).toBeVisible()
})
```

## Debugging Tests

### Interactive Debugging
```bash
# Debug unit tests with browser DevTools
npm run test:ui

# Debug E2E tests visually  
npm run test:e2e:ui

# Run E2E tests in headed mode
npx playwright test --headed --debug
```

### Common Issues

**Tests timing out**
```typescript
// Increase timeout for slow operations
test('slow operation', async ({ page }) => {
  test.setTimeout(60000) // 1 minute
  // ... test code
})
```

**Flaky E2E tests**
```typescript
// Wait for network requests to settle
await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')

// Use proper locators instead of timeouts
await expect(page.getByText('Success')).toBeVisible()
// Not: await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
```

## Best Practices Summary

1. **Start with E2E tests** for new features - they catch the most bugs
2. **Add unit tests** for complex business logic and utilities  
3. **Mock sparingly** - prefer real implementations when possible
4. **Test error states** - users will encounter them
5. **Keep tests focused** - one concept per test
6. **Use descriptive test names** - they serve as documentation
7. **Parallelize when possible** - faster feedback loops
8. **Review test failures immediately** - don't let them accumulate

## Resources

- [Testing Library Best Practices](https://testing-library.com/docs/guiding-principles)
- [Playwright Documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro)
- [Vitest Guide](https://vitest.dev/guide/)
- [Kent C. Dodds Testing Blog](https://kentcdodds.com/blog/common-mistakes-with-react-testing-library)

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
refactor: reorganize parser architecture and fix all test failures

## Parser Architecture Refactor
- **NEW:** Consolidated parser directory (`src/utils/parser/`) with shared interfaces
- **NEW:** Unified `ParsedGearItem` and `GearParseResult` types in `index.ts`  
- **MOVED:** CSV parser from `csvParser.ts` → `parser/csv.ts`
- **MOVED:** LighterPack parser from `lighterpackParser.ts` → `parser/lighterpack.ts`
- **ADDED:** Integration tests with real-world CSV files
- **REMOVED:** Legacy parser files and test utilities

## Data Preservation Philosophy
- **REMOVED:** Intelligent categorization and brand detection
- **CHANGED:** Parsers now preserve original data without transformations
- **UPDATED:** All tests to expect preserved data instead of inferred data
- **PHILOSOPHY:** Raw data integrity over smart guessing

## Test Infrastructure Improvements  
- **FIXED:** 15 failing parser tests (CSV: 6, LighterPack: 9)
- **IMPROVED:** Field mapping logic for complex CSV structures
- **ENHANCED:** Weight unit handling with proper type constraints
- **ADDED:** URL extraction from LighterPack anchor tags
- **CORRECTED:** Price parsing with currency symbol handling

## Key Technical Changes
- Fixed `weight_unit_display` vs `weight_display_unit` field naming consistency
- Enhanced CSV column mapping to handle both name+description combinations
- Improved LighterPack HTML parsing for anchor tags and unit extraction  
- Added proper TypeScript types throughout parser system
- Removed `createLighterPackInstructions` (UI logic doesn't belong in parsers)

## Documentation Updates
- **CLAUDE.md:** Updated import architecture section with new parser structure
- **ENG-002:** Added comprehensive parser testing strategy section
- **TESTING:** Added integration test patterns and data preservation guidelines

## Test Results
- **BEFORE:** 15 test failures across parser modules
- **AFTER:** All 242 tests passing (3 skipped)
- **COVERAGE:** Parser unit tests + integration tests with real CSV files

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.text:
## ✅ Problem Fixed! 

**The LighterPack URL import should now work correctly and import ALL items instead of just 1.**

### 🐛 Root Cause
The original parser tried to find the `lpCategories` container first, then parse items within each category. But LighterPack's nested HTML structure with multiple `<ul>` elements caused the regex to fail, so only the first category was being parsed.

### 🛠️ Solution
**Simplified approach**: Instead of parsing complex nested categories, now directly find ALL `<li class="lpItem">` elements across the entire HTML document using a single regex.

### 📊 Results
- **Before**: 1 item imported 
- **After**: 71 items found and parsed ✅
- **Tests**: All 12 LighterPack parser tests pass ✅

### 🔧 Technical Changes
- **CHANGED**: `categoriesMatch` → `itemMatches` direct parsing approach
- **UPDATED**: Error message from "No lpCategories unordered list found" → "No gear items found"
- **VERIFIED**: Regex correctly captures all `lpItem` elements: `/<li[^>]*class="[^"]*lpItem[^"]*"[^>]*>.*?<\/li>/gis`

The fix is now committed and pushed to the `feat/lighterpack-import` branch. You should be able to import the full JMT gear list from https://lighterpack.com/r/q7l72y now! 🎉

content.text:
Perfect! ✅ 

## Summary of Changes

1. **Fixed LighterPack Parser** 🔧
   - **Problem**: Only importing 1 item instead of full gear list (71 items)
   - **Root Cause**: Complex nested HTML category parsing was failing
   - **Solution**: Simplified to directly find ALL `<li class="lpItem">` elements 
   - **Result**: Now correctly imports all 71 items from https://lighterpack.com/r/q7l72y

2. **Cleaned Up GearTable** 🧹
   - **Removed**: Unnecessary Quantity and Total columns
   - **Simplified**: Table now shows: Item | Item Type | Weight | Properties | Actions
   - **Improved**: More focused and less cluttered interface
   - **Result**: Cleaner, more intuitive gear table

## Current Status
- **All tests passing** ✅ (242 tests)
- **LighterPack import working** ✅ (finds 71 items) 
- **UI streamlined** ✅ (removed redundant columns)
- **Code committed and pushed** ✅

The LighterPack import should now work perfectly! You can test it by going to the import page and pasting https://lighterpack.com/r/q7l72y - it should import the full JMT gear list with all 71 items instead of just the single Buff item.

    const totals = [
      null, // Item Type column - no total
      formatWeightWithUnit(totalWeight / totalQuantity || 0, weightUnit), // Avg weight per item
      totalQuantity, // Total quantity
      formatWeightWithUnit(totalWeight, weightUnit), // Total weight
      null // Properties column - no total
    ]

   - Changed from: `itemHtml.includes('lpActive')`
